abstract.title: ABSTRACT
abstract.p: The rising incidence and mortality of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) present a significant public health challenge. Histidine, an essential amino acid, plays a pivotal role in metabolic processes, yet its specific contribution to LUAD pathogenesis remains to be elucidated. This study obtained bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data for LUAD from UCSC Xena and Code Ocean platforms, respectively. By integrating differential expression analysis, univariate/multivariate Cox analysis, and LASSO regression analysis, prognostic genes for LUAD were identified, and a prognostic risk model was constructed. Algorithms including ESTIMATE, ssGSEA, and CIBERSORT were employed to investigate immune heterogeneity across different groups. Furthermore, molecular subtypes of LUAD were identified through consensus clustering. This study, through the integration of bulk and scRNA-seq data, identified epithelial cells as the key effector cell population in LUAD, which can be further subdivided into four functionally heterogeneous subpopulations. Seven histidine metabolism-related epithelial cell-specific genes with prognostic significance in LUAD were identified (WIF1, GATA2, CD69, ID1, C4BPA, WFDC2, and CCL20), enabling the construction of a robust prognostic risk model. Immune infiltration analysis revealed that low-risk patients exhibited more robust immune infiltration and activity. Furthermore, cross-cancer exploratory evidence suggested potential sensitivity to CTLA-4 and PD-L1 inhibitors in this group. Furthermore, consensus clustering analysis successfully partitioned LUAD into two molecular subtypes exhibiting immune heterogeneity. The prognostic model constructed based on epithelial cell-specific genes associated with histidine metabolism effectively distinguishes LUAD patients and their immune characteristics, revealing epithelial cells as a key cell population regulating LUAD histidine metabolism.

list-item.p: This study identified seven epithelial cell-specific genes associated with histidine metabolism (WIF1, GATA2, CD69, ID1, C4BPA, WFDC2, and CCL20) related to the prognosis of LUAD, and based on this, a robust prognostic risk model for LUAD was constructed.

Based on seven epithelial cell-specific genes associated with histidine metabolism, this study successfully classified LUAD into two different molecular subtypes, and significant immune heterogeneity was exhibited among the subtypes.
Epithelial cells are the key effector cell population in LUAD and can be further divided into four subpopulations with distinct functions.

sec.title: Introduction
sec.p: Lung cancer is the primary driver of cancer-related mortality globally, and its pathological types mainly include small cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) [1]. Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) as the most common subtype of NSCLC, has shown an increasing trend in morbidity and mortality in recent years [2]. Patients with early-stage LUAD typically achieve favourable outcomes and a relatively good prognosis following surgical intervention [1]. However, a significant proportion of patients remain prone to recurrence or metastasis postoperatively, ultimately leading to treatment failure [3]. With the application of targeted drugs and immunotherapy, survival outcomes for LUAD patients have significantly improved [4,5]. Nevertheless, limitations in target selection and the emergence of drug resistance remain major obstacles in current clinical treatment [6]. Therefore, in-depth exploration of treatment targets and targeted drugs specific to LUAD has become a critical issue requiring urgent resolution in this field.

Metabolic reprogramming is central to the initiation and advancement of tumours, including the active alteration of intracellular metabolic fluxes by tumour cells to meet increased synthetic and energy demands [7]; abnormal accumulation of metabolites can directly promote tumorigenesis [8]. Histidine, as an essential amino acid, is extensively involved in multiple physiological processes and metabolic pathways [9]. Recent studies indicate that histidine and its metabolites are closely associated with cancer progression [10]. For instance, a histamine-producing probiotic (Lactobacillus reuteri hdc+) reduces the number and size of colonic tumours while decreasing levels of pro-inflammatory cytokines in the colonic mucosa [11]; Upregulation of histamine H2 subtype receptor expression correlates with improved survival in colorectal cancer patients [12], while the histamine H4 receptor plays a crucial role in inhibiting epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in NSCLC [13]. Furthermore, degradation products of histidine, such as uric acid, glutamic acid, and cisuric acid, exhibit immunosuppressive properties and may promote tumour progression by inhibiting antitumor immune function [14]. These studies highlight the potential clinical translational value of novel therapeutic strategies targeting histidine metabolism.

To elucidate the potential role of histidine metabolism-related genes (HMRGs) in LUAD, this study identified key cell subpopulations with active histidine metabolism based on single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data and employed pseudotime analysis to reveal their dynamic evolutionary trajectories. By integrating publicly available TCGA data, we further identified LUAD prognosis-associated genes and constructed a molecular tool for patient prognosis risk stratification. Based on key prognostic markers, we established a novel molecular subtype classification system, systematically elucidating the heterogeneity of immune infiltration patterns across different subtypes. This study aims to provide new insights into the biological basis of prognosis differences among LUAD patients under current standard treatments.

sec.title: Data source
sec.p: The RNA-Seq data utilized for model training in this study were sourced from the UCSC Xena database (https://xena.ucsc.edu/), specifically the TCGA-LUAD cohort comprising 59 normal and 526 tumour samples. This study acquired copy number alteration profiles from TCGA portal (https://portal.gdc.cancer.gov/). The validation dataset was acquired from the publicly accessible GEO repository (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/), comprising: GSE11969 (Tumour: 90) and GSE13213 (Tumour: 117). To minimize the impact of batch effects and ensure cross-study comparability, inter-array normalization was performed for training and validation datasets using the normalizeBetweenArrays function within the limma R package (v3.62.2). Based on research by Mariathasan et al. [15], we utilized the IMvigor210 cohort, which comprises patients with metastatic urothelial carcinoma treated with atezolizumab, a therapeutic anti-programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) agent. Immunophenoscore (IPS) data for LUAD were sourced from the TCIA database (https://tcia.at). Additionally, scRNA-seq data for LUAD were obtained from the Code Ocean platform (https://codeocean.com/capsule/8321305/tree/v1), which included 10 tumour cases and 10 normal cases. A search for the keyword ‘KEGG_HISTIDINE_METABOLISM’ was performed in the MSigDB database (https://www.gsea-msigdb.org/gsea/msigdb), which yielded a total of 29 HMRGs (Supplementary Table S1).

sec.title: Candidate key cell clusters were identified
sec.p: Drawing on scRNA-seq data from LUAD, the seurat package (v4.3.0) was used to filter data to ensure the quality of analysis results, including: cells with fewer than 500 or more than 10,000 gene expression features, cells with fewer than 1000 or more than 100,000 unique molecular identifier, cells with mitochondrial gene expression exceeding 30%, and cells with haemoglobin gene expression exceeding 5%. Data normalization was performed using the SCTransform package. Principal component analysis (PCA) was performed for dimensionality reduction, selecting the principal component with a resolution parameter of 0.8. Perform unsupervised clustering analysis using the FindNeighbors and FindClusters functions to divide cells into multiple independent clusters. The clustering results were visualized using the Uniform Manifold Approximation and Projection (UMAP) technique and annotated based on representative marker genes. Based on HMRGs, compute the AUCell Score for cells using the AUCell package, then stratify cells into high- and low-score groups utilizing the median. Additionally, this study employed the CellChat software package to systematically infer and analyse intercellular communication networks among cell clusters in the high- and low-scoring groups for histidine metabolism, based on a ligand-receptor interaction model. The netAnalysis_computeCentLUADlity function was used to calculate network centrality, identifying ligands and receptors within CellChat.

sec.title: Identification and reannotation of key cell clusters
sec.p: To characterize key histidine metabolism-related epithelial cell clusters, this study employed the FindAllMarkers function to perform differential expression analysis on tumour and control groups of epithelial cell clusters. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified using a threshold of |logFC| >0.585 and a corrected p-value < 0.05. The clusterProfiler package (v4.14.6) was applied to perform GO and KEGG enrichment analyses on the DEGs. Unsupervised clustering analysis was performed utilizing the Seurat package on the identified key cell clusters, which were annotated drawing on marker expression. For epithelial cell clusters, reannotation was performed using the Seurat package. Pseudotime analysis was conducted with the monocle2 package to calculate pseudo-time values and reconstruct cellular developmental trajectories and states.

sec.title: Development and validation of a prognostic model for LUAD
sec.p: To further construct a prognostic risk model for LUAD, we combined key characteristic genes identified in epithelial cells with DEGs obtained from TCGA-LUAD cohort analysis (tumour vs. control: limma package; threshold: |logFC| >1 and adjusted p-value < 0.05). An intersection analysis was performed to identify shared features. LUAD prognostic genes were further screened using univariate Cox analysis (survival package), least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression analysis (glmnet package), and multivariate Cox analysis (survival package). A prognostic model based on LUAD prognostic genes was constructed via stepwise regression. The risk score calculation method is as follows:Riskscore=∑(Geneexpressioni×Coefficienti)
The prognostic model’s performance was assessed in both the training and validation cohorts employing Kaplan-Meier (K-M) survival analysis and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis.

sec.title: Construction of nomogram
sec.p: Drawing on prognostic gene signatures, along with clinical features and RiskScore, both univariate and multivariate Cox analyses were conducted, and a nomogram was developed for predicting LUAD risk. The clinical utility of the model in predicting 1-, 3-, and 5-year outcomes was assessed utilizing calibration curves.

sec.title: Immune infiltration analysis
sec.p: This study analysed immune cell infiltration across different groups using MCPcounter, ssGSEA, and CIBERSORT algorithms. The ESTIMATE algorithm was employed to calculate the Stromal, Immune, and ESTIMATE scores for each comparison group, and tumour purity was determined. Using the IMvigor210 cohort, we categorized displayed stable disease (SD) and progressive disease (PD) as non-response (NR), and complete response (CR) and partial response (PR) as response (R) to analyse response rates to anti-PD-L1 blockade across different risk groups. IPS for LUAD were retrieved from the TCIA database to predict response capacity to anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-L1 therapies in different risk cohorts.

sec.title: Tumour mutational burden profiling (TMB) and drug sensitivity analysis
sec.p: The mutational landscape was characterized in the TCGA-LUAD cohort to delineate the top 20 mutated genes in different risk. For pharmacogenomic profiling, half-maximal inhibitory concentrations (IC50) of LUAD relevant chemotherapeutics were quantified utilizing pRRophetic package (v0.5). The CellMiner database (https://discover.nci.nih.gov/cellminer/) was applied to screen and identify anticancer drugs associated with prognostic genes, and spearman analysis was utilized for evaluate the correlation between gene expression and drug sensitivity.

sec.title: Molecular typing of LUAD
sec.p: Consensus clustering (ConsensusClusterPlus package, v1.70.0) stratified LUAD into distinct molecular subtypes drawing on prognostic genes, with clustering stability assessed via cumulative distribution function (CDF) and delta area curve analyses. Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed to evaluate the independent prognostic value of the molecular subtypes.

sec.title: Data analysis
sec.p: R software (version 4.4.0) was applied to data analysis and visualization. Wilcoxon test was utilized for inter-group comparison. Pearson correlation coefficient was used to quantify the correlation, and the threshold of statistical significance was set at p < 0.05.

sec.title: Screening of key cell clusters in LUAD
sec.p:
We performed unsupervised clustering analysis on 33 principal components (Figure 1A) and annotated 114,489 cells into eight distinct cell types based on classical marker genes (Figure 1B,C). Results indicate that clusters 0, 2, 5, 12, 10, 29, and 32 represent T cell; clusters 16, 18, 4, 20, 27, 15, 11, 26, 9, and 31 represent epithelial cells. Simultaneously, the cellular composition was compared between normal and tumour samples, revealing an increased proportion of epithelial cells and a decreased proportion of macrophage in the tumour group compared to the normal group (Figure 1D). Gene expression heatmap results indicated that HMRGs were highly expressed in epithelial cells compared to other cell clusters (Figure 1E). Subsequently, based on HMRGs, the study calculated the AUCell Score for the eight cell types in tumour samples (Figure 1F,G). Epithelial cells not only exhibited a higher AUCell Score (Figure 1H), but also constituted a significantly larger proportion in the high-score group (Figure 1I). Next, this study conducted a cell communication analysis to investigate differences in cell cluster interactions between high- and low-scoring groups in histidine metabolism. First, we compared and visualized the number of cell-cell communication events and their interaction strengths between the two groups (Figure 1J), revealing that the low-score group significantly exceeded the high-score group in both aspects. Furthermore, by displaying the number and interaction strength of communication events between different cell types (Figure 1K), results showed that compared to the low-score group, the high-score group exhibited upregulation in both the number and interaction strength of communication events between epithelial cells and smc. Subsequently, comparing heatmaps of the top 10 input and output signalling pathways between high- and low-scoring groups (Figure 1L,M) revealed enhanced MK signalling pathway output in epithelial cells within the low-score group, alongside increased MIF signalling pathway input. This pattern starkly contrasted with the high-score group, suggesting divergent key signalling mechanisms between the two sample cohorts. Specifically, compared to the Low group with reduced histidine metabolic activity, the High group exhibits increased quantity and intensity of epithelial cell communication. The above findings suggest that epithelial cells may play a key role in the malignant progression of LUAD through the histidine metabolic pathway. Therefore, subsequent analyses will focus on epithelial cells. Figure 1.

sec.title: Comprehensive characterization of key epithelial cell subpopulations
sec.p:
To characterize key histidine metabolism-related epithelial cell clusters, we performed differential expression analysis to identify epithelial cell features associated with histidine metabolism. These genes correlate with histidine metabolic activity (Supplementary Figure S1A). To further elucidate potential molecular mechanisms, we performed gene enrichment analysis. Gene enrichment analysis indicated that these genes were significantly enriched in biological functions such as protein sequestration activity, molecular sequestration activity, and chemokine receptor binding, and were strongly associated with the NOD-like receptor signalling pathway (Supplementary Figure S1B-C). To further investigate the role of epithelial cells in LUAD, this study classified 25,064 epithelial cells into four subpopulations based on classical markers: AT1, AT2, ciliocytes, and club cells (Figure 2A–C). Analysis of the proportion of these cell subpopulations in tumour versus normal tissue revealed that AT2 cells were most abundant in the tumour group, while AT1 and Ciliated cells were significantly reduced compared to the normal group (Figure 2D). The pseudotime trajectory reveals a transcriptional continuum among epithelial cell populations, characterized by a transition from an AT1-related state through a Club-cell intermediate towards AT2 and Ciliated cell profiles (Figure 2E–G). Furthermore, heatmap analysis (Figure 2H) reveals significant up- or down-regulation patterns of key genes during cell differentiation from state2 to state1 and state3. Figure 2.

sec.title: Screening of prognostic genes in LUAD
sec.p:
This study conducted the following analyses to screen genes associated with LUAD prognosis. First, differential analysis was performed on the training set data utilizing a screening threshold (|logFC| >1, adjusted p-value < 0.05), yielding 1619 LUAD_DEGs (Figure 3A). Intersecting these genes with epithelial cell-specific DEGs associated with histidine metabolism identified 80 common DEGs (Figure 3B). Subsequently, 34 candidate prognostic genes were identified through univariate Cox analysis (Figure 3C), followed by LASSO regression analysis to refine the list to 12 genes (Figure 3D). Ultimately, seven LUAD prognostic genes were identified through multivariate Cox analysis (Figure 3E). These genes exhibited significant expression across different samples: WFDC2 and CCL20 were significantly upregulated in tumour tissues, while the remaining five genes were significantly downregulated (Figure 3F). sec.title: Development and validation of a prognostic model for LUAD
sec.p: This study constructed a prognostic model for LUAD based on seven prognostic genes. The risk score calculation formula is as follows:Riskscore=−0.060×WIF1+0.140×ID1+0.104×CCL20−0.148×GATA2−0.192×CD69−0.133×WFDC2−0.069×C4BPA

The expression levels and independent prognostic value of the seven prognostic genes showed significant differences across risk groups, and were associated with the expression levels of genes related to histidine metabolism (Supplementary Figure S2A-C). To assess the model’s robustness, this study validated it using training data (TCGA-LUAD) and validation datasets (GSE11969 and GSE13213). ROC curve analysis demonstrated robust predictive capability across the training set and both validation sets (Figure 4A). Further K-M survival analysis revealed (Figure 4B) that low-risk patients exhibited markedly longer survival durations than high-risk patients in both the training and validation sets. To investigate biological characteristics between risk groups, gene enrichment analysis was performed. The results (Figure 4C) revealed differences between the two groups across multiple categories: MF such as endopeptidase activity, endopeptidase activity, and organic acid binding; biological processes (BP) including induction of bacterial agglutination, antibacterial humoral response, and defence response to bacterium; and cellular components (CC) like clathrin-coated endocytic vesicle, late endosome, and multivesicular body. Furthermore, based on scRNA-seq data, this study employed the AUCell Score to evaluate the activity levels of 7 prognostic genes across various cell types. Cells were stratified into high- and low-score groups based on the median AUCell Score (Figure 4D), with epithelial cells exhibiting the highest AUCell Score relative to other cell types (Figure 4E). Further analysis revealed that epithelial cells not only exhibited significantly higher AUCell Scores in the high-score group compared to the low-score group (Figure 4F), but also constituted the largest proportion within this group (Figure 4G). sec.title: Construction and validation of a LUAD prognostic nomogram
sec.p:
This study investigated the association between clinical characteristics and risk scores, revealing that male patients exhibited significantly higher risk scores than female patients, the T3+T4 group showed significantly higher scores than the T1+T2 group, Stage III+IV group had significantly higher scores than Stage I+II group, and N1-3 group significantly higher than N0 group (Figure 5A). Univariate Cox analysis indicated that riskScore, stage, M, N, and T classification were all significant prognostic predictors (Figure 5B). Multivariate Cox analysis further revealed that riskScore, T, and N were key prognostic predictors (Figure 5C). To predict survival probability in LUAD patients, we developed a nomogram integrating riskScore with key clinical parameters (Figure 5D). Calibration curve analysis validated the model’s predictive accuracy, demonstrating its clinical utility in forecasting 1-, 3-, and 5-year survival rates (Figure 5E). Figure 5.

sec.title: Immune infiltration analysis
sec.p:
To investigate the immune characteristics in different risk groups, the following analyses were conducted. ssGSEA immune infiltration analysis revealed that most immune cells and immune functions exhibited significantly higher infiltration levels in the low-risk group compared to the high-risk group (Figure 6A,B). ESTIMATE algorithm analysis indicated that patients in the low-risk group exhibited higher Stromal/Immune/ESTIMATE Score, with lower TumorPurity (Figure 6B). Gene expression analysis demonstrated that most immune checkpoints were upregulated in the low-risk group (Figure 6C). Additionally, the high-risk group exhibited significantly higher TIDE scores (p = 2.9e-07), with a moderate effect size (r = 0.23), suggesting greater potential for immune escape (Figure 6D). Note that TIDE scores predict immune-evasion tendency and do not directly measure clinical response. Correspondingly, exploratory analysis in an external immunotherapy cohort indicated that the low-risk group is associated with higher response rates to anti-PD-L1 blockade, providing cross-cancer exploratory evidence for the potential therapeutic benefit of this signature (Figure 6E). IPS analysis further indicated that this group exhibited stronger responsiveness to both anti-CTLA-4 and anti-PD-L1 therapies (Figure 6F). Figure 6.

sec.title: TMB and drug sensitivity analysis
sec.p:
The frequency of somatic gene mutations was assessed across different risk groups via TMB analysis (Figure 7A), revealing a significantly higher TP53 mutation rate in high-risk patients (26%) compared to low-risk patients (21%). Further analysis demonstrated that the tumour burden mutation levels in the high-risk group were significantly higher than those in the low-risk group (Figure 7B). In sensitivity analysis for four commonly used LUAD chemotherapeutic agents (Figure 7C), the IC50 value for gefitinib was significantly higher in the low-risk group than in the high-risk group, whereas the opposite was true for crizotinib, erlotinib, and dabrafenib. Additionally, correlation analysis revealed (Figure 7D, Supplementary Table S2): ID1 expression negatively correlated with sensitivity to hypothemycin and dabrafenib; GATA2 expression positively correlated with imatinib sensitivity; and WFDC2 expression positively correlated with acetalax sensitivity. sec.title: Molecular subtypes of LUAD
sec.p:
This study classified LUAD into two molecular subtypes (group1 and group2) drawing on prognostic genes using consensus clustering (Figure 8A). The robustness of this classification was validated through CDF and delta area curve analysis (Figure 8B,C). Gene expression analysis revealed that WIF1, GATA2, CD69, ID1, C4BPA, and WFDC2 were significantly upregulated in group2 (Figure 8D). K-M survival analysis demonstrated significantly higher survival rates in group2 patients compared to group1 patients (Figure 8E). Univariate Cox regression analysis showed that both the molecular subtype and clinical stage were significantly associated with overall survival (p < 0.05, Supplementary Figure S3A). Furthermore, multivariate Cox analysis confirmed that the molecular subtype remained a significant independent prognostic factor (p < 0.05) after adjusting for age, gender, and stage (Supplementary Figure S3B). Subsequent KEGG and GO enrichment analysis of DEGs between the two groups revealed significant differences in multiple biological processes, including mitotic nuclear division and sister chromatid segregation (Figure 8F). Furthermore, immune cell infiltration analysis using the MCP-counter algorithm (Figure 8G) revealed differences in infiltration levels of endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and neutrophils in different groups. Analysis based on the ssGSEA algorithm (Figure 8H) showed higher infiltration levels of CD8+ T cells, NK cells, and MHC class I in group1. Analysis using the CIBERSORT algorithm (Figure 8I) revealed significantly higher infiltration levels of Macrophages M0, Macrophages M1, and T cells CD4 memory activated in group1 compared to group2. Collectively, the two LUAD subtypes identified in this study exhibit distinct heterogeneity in immune microenvironment characteristics and molecular functions. Figure 8.

sec.title: Discussion
sec.p: As the most prevalent subtype of NSCLC, the increasing incidence and mortality of LUAD have become a significant public health challenge [2]. Histidine and its metabolites are closely implicated in cancer progression [10]. However, the mechanism of action between the two has not yet been fully clarified. This study established a LUAD prognostic prediction model based on seven HMRGs, demonstrating robust stability and independence in prognostic assessment. By integrating single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data, it further revealed the pivotal role of HMRGs in LUAD progression and tumour microenvironment regulation.

This study identified seven HMRGs as prognostic-related genes in LUAD (WIF1, GATA2, CD69, ID1, C4BPA, WFDC2, and CCL20), which are extensively involved in tumorigenesis and progression. Consistent with our findings, previous literature reports that GATA binding protein 2 (GATA2) [16], the CD69 molecule (CD69) [17], and Inhibitor of DNA binding 1 (ID1) [18] exhibit low expression in LUAD patient tissues, while WAP four-disulphide core domain 2 (WFDC2) shows high expression [19]. Wnt inhibitory factor 1 (WIF1), a key component of the Wnt signalling pathway, exhibits promoter hypermethylation that not only contributes to abnormal Wnt pathway activation in NSCLC but also serves as an auxiliary diagnostic biomarker for NSCLC-associated malignant pleural effusion [20]. C-C motif chemokine ligand 20 (CCL20) participates in multiple carcinogenic processes, and its knockdown inhibits EMT processes and cell proliferation in LUAD cells both in vitro and in vivo [21]. Collectively, these HMRGs may play critical roles in LUAD initiation and progression and hold potential value as prognostic biomarkers.

This study classified epithelial cells in LUAD into four subtypes: alveolar type I cells (AT1), alveolar type II cells (AT2), ciliated cells, and club cells. Among these, club and ciliated cells are primarily distributed in the proximal airways, while AT1 and AT2 cells are located in the alveolar walls, and AT2 cells have a critical function in maintaining alveolar homoeostasis and repairing damage [22]. They possess self-renewal capacity and can differentiate into stem cell-like cells following injury or genetic mutation [23,24]. Early-stage cancer cells dedifferentiate into a stem cell-like state highly similar to AT2 cells, termed AT2-like cells [25]. This may explain the increased proportion of AT2 cells observed in the tumour group in our study. Furthermore, AT2-like cells exhibit distinct metabolic reprogramming features, notably strong expression of ribosomal and mitochondrial-related genes, collectively promoting tumour progression [25]. Whether these cells are associated with the histidine metabolic warrants further investigation.

TMB profiling demonstrated that the high-risk group exhibited a significantly higher frequency of TP53 gene mutations (26%) compared to the low-risk group (21%), suggesting that this mutation may be associated with tumorigenesis. Previous studies have demonstrated that in LUAD, TP53 not only induces highly specific AT1 cell differentiation [26], but its mutation also severely disrupts homoeostasis, leading to malignant progression and poor patient prognosis [27]. Furthermore, TP53 is implicated in multiple metabolic pathways. It influences glycolysis through mechanisms including transcriptional suppression of glucose transporter expression, downregulation of glycolytic rate-limiting enzymes, reduced expression of transporters responsible for lactate efflux, and negative regulation of AKT/mTOR and NF-κB signalling pathways [28]. In breast cancer, TP53 mutations promote energy metabolism reprogramming and enhance glycolysis [29]. Mutant TP53 binds and activates transcription factors SREBPs, inducing expression of multiple genes in the mevalonate pathway to promote cholesterol and isoprenoid synthesis, thereby influencing lipid metabolism [30]. However, whether TP53 mutations contribute to LUAD development by regulating histidine metabolism remains to be further investigated.

Immune cells constitute a critical component of the tumour microenvironment, significantly influencing tumour progression and treatment response [31]. This study employed algorithms such as ssGSEA, CIBERSORT, and ESTIMATE to analyse immune cell infiltration levels, revealing a more active immune microenvironment in the low-risk group. For instance, in contrast to the high-risk group, the low-risk group demonstrated a significantly greater abundance of tumour-infiltrating CD8+ T cells, Tregs, and B cells. Research indicates that CD8+ T cells, as crucial cells in antitumor immunity, can recognize and kill tumour cells [32]. B cells, under tumour and inflammatory conditions, enhance T cell responses by producing antibodies and chemokines, function as local antigen-presenting cells, and assist in forming tertiary lymphoid structures (TLS), thereby sustaining effective immune responses [6,33]. Subsequent analyses revealed significantly higher response rates to PD-L1 inhibitor therapy in low-risk patients compared to high-risk patients. Clinical trial data confirmed that the humanized anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody atezolizumab significantly prolonged overall survival with superior safety profiles compared to docetaxel in patients with advanced NSCLC [34].

This study identified two LUAD molecular subtypes with distinct clinical and biological heterogeneity. Survival analysis demonstrated that patients in Group 1 had a significantly poorer prognosis than those in Group 2. This difference remained statistically significant (p < 0.05) in a multivariate Cox regression analysis after adjusting for age, sex, and clinical stage. These findings confirm that the molecular subtype is an independent prognostic indicator for LUAD. Immune landscape analysis revealed distinct heterogeneity between the two subtypes. Group 1 exhibited a ‘high infiltration, high risk’ profile; despite significantly higher levels of infiltrating CD8+ T cells, NK cells, and M1 macrophages compared to Group 2, these patients experienced a poorer prognosis. Functional enrichment analysis suggests this paradox may stem from hyperactive cell cycle progression – specifically mitotic nuclear division and sister chromatid segregation – where the rapid turnover of malignant cells outpaces the clearance capacity of the immune microenvironment [35]. Conversely, Group 2 demonstrated a marked survival advantage. This subtype was characterized by the significant upregulation of tumour suppressors such as WIF1. As an endogenous antagonist of the Wnt signalling pathway, WIF1 likely limits tumour cell stemness and proliferation [36], enabling Group 2 to maintain lower malignancy and prolonged survival despite relatively lower immune cell infiltration. In summary, these subtypes not only achieve robust risk stratification but also elucidate the dynamic imbalance between oncogenic proliferation and immune surveillance in LUAD.

Although this study conducted a relatively systematic analysis of the HMRGs of LUAD, there are still several limitations. Firstly, the single-cell and bulk RNA-seq data are from public databases, which means that the sample size and patient population are relatively limited. In the future, large-scale, multi-centre cohorts will be needed to verify the universality of these findings. Secondly, the clinical application value of this study still needs to be further verified through various methods. Evaluate the effects of prognostic genes on LUAD cell/animal models through in vivo and in vitro experiments; Explore its mechanism of action at a higher resolution by using spatial transcriptomics technology; Develop in vitro diagnostic kits to enhance the effectiveness of early disease screening and prediction.

sec.title: Conclusion
sec.p: Our study identified seven epithelial cell-specific genes associated with histidine metabolism as potential prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets for LUAD. scRNA-seq data analysis reveals epithelial cells as a key effector cell population, with four functionally heterogeneous subpopulations playing distinct roles in regulating tumour initiation and progression. These findings require further validation through prospective clinical studies and functional experiments before translating into therapeutic applications.
